title: Harness-origin prompt prefixes
description: THE single declaration of what a UserPromptSubmit prompt looks like when the HARNESS raised it rather than a human. The harness raises UserPromptSubmit identically when a backgrounded task completes as when a person types, so origin cannot be read from the event -- only from the text. Every reader that must tell those apart resolves this file; none restates its literals. That constraint is mechanized: a numbered invariant in scripts/validate-enforcement-map.sh fails the build if a shipped file carries one of these strings outside this declaration, and it derives BOTH sides rather than hand-listing either. Written because ai-dlc-pause.sh's own header instructed it -- 'if a broader predicate is ever needed, single-source it, do not copy it' -- after a hand-maintained copy of this list in a second language was the failure it was warning about. Matching is ANCHORED at the start of the prompt, after <system-reminder> blocks are stripped: a prompt that MENTIONS a notification is operator prose about a notification, and dropping it would discard a real steer.

prefixes.description: Anchored prefixes. A prompt whose text starts with any of these was raised by the harness. Measured on the reference consumer at v0.264.0: over its captured request history the set matched 4 of 6 entries and zero operator asks, and over its continuation log it accounted for 4 of 5 USER_PAUSE events.

copy_scan_exempt.description: Prefixes I91's copy-scan does NOT search for, with the exemption declared here rather than buried in the invariant so it is visible to the next reader. (This arm was numbered I76 until the invariant index was derived and showed two unrelated arms holding that one ID; the older claimant, install.sh's skill-root ship/claim join, kept it.) A prefix belongs here when the same literal is also an ordinary transcript-envelope token that unrelated code legitimately handles. Measured, not assumed: scanning for `<command-` reported core/hooks/ai-dlc-acknowledge.sh (greps `<command-name>/ai-dlc</command-name>` to find the last skill invocation) and scripts/ab-lead-model.js (tests `<command-name>/(clear|model|compact|resume)` and sets isOperator TRUE — the opposite polarity). Neither classifies prompt origin; both would be permanently red. The prefix stays in `prefixes` and is still enforced against genuineOperatorText — only the copy-scan skips it.
